usage: • Use 藥草 for herbs and other useful medicinal or culinary plants; it is a countable noun in general English teaching terms, but Cantonese often uses it as a category word rather than a strict single plant name.
• It fits well in plant-and-garden contexts, especially when talking about planting, drying, buying, or using herbs for health or cooking.
• The word sounds natural in written and spoken Cantonese, but in everyday conversation people may also use more specific names for individual herbs when they know them.
• Good learner tip: pair it with words for planting, growing, smelling, or making soup/tea to sound natural in garden and kitchen topics.

examples.sentence: 佢喺花園種咗好多藥草。
examples.jyutping: keoi5 hai2 faa1 jyun4 zung3 zo2 hou2 do1 joek6 cou2.
examples.meaning: He planted a lot of herbs in the garden.

examples.jyutping: ngo5 aa3 maa1 zung1 ji3 maai5 san1 sin1 joek6 cou2.
